recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-6949 unless a future Pharmacy decision intentionally revises MedicationAdministration scope again.
issue_request: FHIR-6949 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request from the 2015May core ballot for MedicationAdministration section 4.14.1. It asked to replace wording that said the resource would principally be used within inpatient settings with wording saying it would principally be used within care settings, including inpatient, because medication administrations occur in all care settings.
initial_application: Git commit fafae8c27e697b5d8280122ab674a8ddaac736a8, '#6949 - updated introduction wording', replaced 'within inpatient settings' with 'within care settings (including inpatient)' in source/medicationadministration/medicationadministration-introduction.xml. This matches the Jira comment recording svn 6317.
additional_context: MedicationAdministration is active in source/fhir.ini, so the introduction source is in current build scope. Later Published issue FHIR-25538 revised the same Scope and Usage paragraph in commit a9dffd224e0795a95e525dd761215701cecf804b by removing 'the capture of' and changing 'intra-venous adjustments' to 'intravenous infusions' while preserving FHIR-6949's care-settings meaning. FHIR-25538 is already represented on the combined branch by 5dadbd95d8cbede56b60c31b985d845d9f86a198. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source/medicationadministration/medicationadministration-introduction.xml says MedicationAdministration is principally used within care settings, including inpatient, and also names outpatient and home-health examples, so the current specification already conveys the requested clarification.
